title: MethScope-Input
text: MethScope uses YAME .cg files methylation input. .cg file compact binary representation methylation data fixed CpG order. running GenerateInput(), query .cg file MRMP reference .cm file must based genome build CpG coordinate order. tutorial shows common input-preparation patterns : BED-like methylation files ALLC files beta methylation fraction tables binary presence/absence tracks complete YAME command documentation, see https://zhou-lab.github.io/YAME/. YAME’s storage guide describes supported CX formats requirement input rows match reference CpG coordinates exactly: https://zhou-lab.github.io/YAME/docs/storage.html. ALLC files, tutorial follows ALLCools definition: https://lhqing.github.io/ALLCools/start/input_files.html.

title: MethScope-Input
text: Use YAME format 3 (-f3) input methylated unmethylated read counts. recommended format bisulfite sequencing data read depth available. Expected input: columns : Align file reference CpG coordinates pack: Check result:
code: chr1    3000826    3000827    4    6 chr1    3001006    3001007    0    8 chrom    start    end    M    U bedtools sort -i sample_mu.bed > sample_mu.sorted.bed  bedtools intersect \   -a cpg_reference.bed.gz \   -b sample_mu.sorted.bed \   -loj \   -sorted | \ awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {if ($8==".") print 0,0; else print $8,$9}' | \ yame pack -f3 - > sample.cg yame info sample.cg yame summary sample.cg

title: MethScope-Input
text: ALLC files tab-separated base-resolution cytosine count tables. ALLCools convention, row 7 mandatory columns header: position 1-based, mc count reads supporting methylation, cov total read coverage. MethScope, convert CG-context rows YAME format 3 setting: command keeps rows whose sequence context begins CG, converts 1-based ALLC position 0-based BED interval, derives U, aligns result CpG reference, packs final two-column M U stream. ALLC file compressed, replace zcat sample.allc.tsv.gz cat sample.allc.tsv.
code: chromosome    position    strand    sequence_context    mc    cov    methylated M = mc U = cov - mc zcat sample.allc.tsv.gz | \ awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}      $4 ~ /^CG/ {        chrom = $1        start = $2 - 1        end = $2        m = $5        u = $6 - $5        if (u < 0) u = 0        print chrom, start, end, m, u      }' | \ bedtools sort -i - > sample_mu.sorted.bed  bedtools intersect \   -a cpg_reference.bed.gz \   -b sample_mu.sorted.bed \   -loj \   -sorted | \ awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {if ($8==".") print 0,0; else print $8,$9}' | \ yame pack -f3 - > sample.cg

title: MethScope-Input
text: Use YAME format 4 (-f4) input already contains methylation fractions beta values. Missing CpGs encoded NA. Expected input: Convert .cg: Format 4 stores methylation fractions retain read depth.
code: chr1    3000826    3000827    0.42 chr1    3001006    3001007    0.81 bedtools sort -i sample_beta.bed > sample_beta.sorted.bed  bedtools intersect \   -a cpg_reference.bed.gz \   -b sample_beta.sorted.bed \   -loj \   -sorted | \ awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {if ($8==".") print "NA"; else print $8}' | \ yame pack -f4 - > sample_beta.cg

title: MethScope-Input
text: Use YAME format 0 (-fb) CpG represented present absent. useful binary tracks, peak overlaps, binarized methylation states.
code: bedtools sort -i binary_track.bed > binary_track.sorted.bed  bedtools intersect \   -a cpg_reference.bed.gz \   -b binary_track.sorted.bed \   -sorted \   -c | \ cut -f4 | \ awk '{if ($1 > 0) print 1; else print 0}' | \ yame pack -fb - > binary_track.cg

text: Estimate cell-type proportions using nnls_deconv(). Bundled reference matrices available inst/extdata, including mm10_Liu2021_ref.rds hg38_Zhou2025_ref.rds.
code: reference_pattern <- "mm10_Liu2021.cm" reference_input <- readRDS("inst/extdata/mm10_Liu2021_ref.rds")  # Imputation is needed before deconvolution if input_pattern contains missing values. input_pattern <- imputeRowMean(input_pattern)  cell_proportion <- nnls_deconv(reference_input, input_pattern)

title: MethScope-Tutorial
text: generating input_pattern, can cluster standard single-cell pipelines.
code: library(Seurat) Pattern.obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = t(input_pattern), assay = "DNAm") VariableFeatures(Pattern.obj) <- rownames(Pattern.obj[['DNAm']]) DefaultAssay(Pattern.obj) <- "DNAm" Pattern.obj <- NormalizeData(Pattern.obj, assay = "DNAm", verbose = FALSE) Pattern.obj <- ScaleData(Pattern.obj, assay = "DNAm", verbose = FALSE) # You can also directly use the initial counts matrix Pattern.obj@assays$DNAm@layers$scale.data <- as.matrix(Pattern.obj@assays$DNAm@layers$counts) Pattern.obj <- RunPCA(Pattern.obj, assay = "DNAm", reduction.name = "mpca", verbose = FALSE) Pattern.obj <- FindNeighbors(Pattern.obj, reduction = "mpca", dims = 1:30) Pattern.obj <- FindClusters(Pattern.obj, verbose = FALSE, resolution = 0.7) Pattern.obj <- RunUMAP(Pattern.obj, reduction = "mpca", reduction.name = "meth.umap", dims = 1:30)

code: # create masked replicates (masked CpGs encoded as 2) # this generate 100 replicates per original sample, each of the 10 output files contains 10 replicates per sample parallel -j 24 'yame dsample -p {} -s {} -r 10 -N 29000 -o example_rep{}.cg example.cg' ::: {1..10}  # summarize MRMP features per replicate parallel -j 24 'yame summary -m patterns.cm example_rep{}.cg | cut -f2,4,10 | doawk | sort -k1,1 -k2,2n | bedtools groupby -g 1 -c 3 -o collapse > example_rep{}_mrmp.txt' ::: {1..10}  cat example_rep*_mrmp.txt > input_pattern.txt  # whole-genome .cg file can be divided into 10k-CpG blocks, and then CpG-level truth from .cg parallel -j 72 'yame rowsub -I {}_10000 example.cg | yame unpack -a - >truth/example_{}.txt' ::: {0..2940} x <- read.table("input_pattern.txt", header = FALSE)  y <- read.table("example_0.txt", header = FALSE) y <- t(y)  # samples x CpGs

title: MethScope-Tutorial
text: Recommended trainning setup: Loss: masked BCEWithLogitsLoss (ignore entries label 2) Optimizer: Adam (lr = 1e-3, weight_decay = 1e-5) Scheduler: ReduceLROnPlateau Model selection: run 3 epoches save checkpoint best validation
code: import torch import torch.nn as nn  class BottleneckDecoder(nn.Module):     def __init__(self, input_dim=num_of_patterns, hidden_dim=512, output_dim=10000):         super().__init__()         self.net = nn.Sequential(             nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),             nn.ReLU(),             nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),             nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)         )     def forward(self, x):         return self.net(x)
